headline: 3-of-6 multisig (Tether-controlled) holds T1 powers (mint, upgrade proxy, blocklist+destroy, admin change) with zero timelock on Ethereum/Arbitrum/Polygon XAUt proxies

findings.text: Ethereum XAUt proxy (0x68749665ff8d2d112fa859aa293f07a622782f38) owner is 3-of-6 multisig at 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828 (https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828 shows getOwners + required=3); implementation (0x4c0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566) has owner() + mint + addToBlockedList + destroyBlockedFunds + transferOwnership[](https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x4c0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566). Same pattern on Arbitrum proxy (0x40461291347e1ecbb09499f3371d3f17f10d7159, owner 0x4DFF9b5b0143E642a3F63a5bcf2d1C328e600bf8 per address_book).

TransparentUpgradeableProxy on ETH/ARB (upgradeTo/upgradeToAndCall/changeAdmin present; admin() reverted on read but proxy owner role per address_book and surfaced links); implementation is non-proxy logic contract (https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x68749665ff8d2d112fa859aa293f07a622782f38 and https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x4c0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566). No timelock or governor contract surfaced.

Execution path: multisig submit/confirm/execute (direct, 0s delay). No MIN_DELAY, timelock, or governor queue/execute path found in any read or surfacer (https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828; no governance contracts in address_book or website).

Primary multisig: 3-of-6 at 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828 (owners listed, required=3, 5382 txs, MAX_OWNER_COUNT=50; https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828). Powers: proxy upgrade/admin change, token owner (mint, blocklist add/remove, destroyBlockedFunds, transferOwnership). Signer identities unknown (no public announcement; likely Tether insiders). No other multisigs or emergency roles surfaced.
No separate emergency-pause/guardian role or time-capped multisig; only the main 3-of-6 multisig controls all privileged functions (no paused() in ABI or state).

Highest tier T1 on uncontested fast path: mint(address,uint256), upgradeTo (replace impl of fund-holding token), destroyBlockedFunds (drain user funds), changeAdmin (replace upgrade admin with EOA) — all callable by the 3-of-6 multisig with no delay or on-chain governance.

steelman.red: 3-of-6 multisig (fails Security Council criteria: <7 signers, unknown/insider composition) can unilaterally mint, upgrade implementation, blocklist+destroy user funds, and change proxy admin with zero timelock or exit window — classic T1 single-party control surface.
steelman.orange: Multisig threshold provides some distribution vs pure EOA, and on-chain transparency of owners/transactions exists, but still fast-path T1 without 7-day bar or broad governance.
steelman.green: No single EOA; multisig requires 3 confirmations and is content-addressed on defipunkd; token is simple ERC-20 with no complex governance attack surface.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because T1 powers (mint, upgrade, destroyBlockedFunds, admin change) are held by a 3-of-6 multisig with direct execution and zero timelock or on-chain governance path, meeting red criteria exactly (C1/C2/C3/C4/C7 evidence from defipunkd reads and address_book).

evidence.shows: 3-of-6 multisig (getOwners + required=3) that owns the XAUt proxy per address_book; controls upgrade/mint/blocklist path; 6 owners listed, no timelock.
TransparentUpgradeableProxy for XAUt; points to implementation 0x4c0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566; upgrade/admin functions present; owner role per address_book is the multisig.
Implementation logic: owner(), mint(), addToBlockedList(), destroyBlockedFunds(), transferOwnership(); no pause(); T1 functions directly callable by owner (multisig).
No on-chain governance, timelock, or decentralized control mentioned; redemption/mint handled off-chain by TG Commodities (Tether entity).

unknowns: C3: no timelock or governor contract discovered after reading proxy/implementation and multisig; assumed absent.
C4: multisig signer identities and insider status unknown (no public disclosure or on-chain labeling); assumed Tether insiders for grading.
C5: no on-chain governance (Governor, token voting, or proposal system) present in any surfacer or website.
C6: no evidence of separate emergency role or time cap; only main multisig path.

headline: On-chain transfers permissionless but no on-chain redeem/exit; physical gold redemption requires off-chain KYC+approval by Tether entity; admin can blocklist+destroy funds with no time cap or escape hatch

findings.text: User-facing on-chain exit/transfer: standard ERC-20 transfer/transferFrom/approve (no dedicated withdraw/redeem/burn for users in ABI); off-chain redeem for physical gold or USD via TG Commodities app[](https://gold.tether.to/faq).

On-chain transfer functions have no pause/onlyRole/whenNotPaused modifiers (ABI shows no paused() or access control beyond owner for mint/block); off-chain redeem requires login+KYC+account verification before request placement or claim.

No pause guard or PAUSE_ROLE in any contract (no paused()/isPaused in proxy or implementation reads); blocklist allows owner (multisig) to addToBlockedList and destroyBlockedFunds indefinitely with no time cap[](https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x4c0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566).
No emergency vs governance pause distinction; only privileged block+destroy by multisig (no time cap, no auto-expiry). Off-chain redemption fully gated by Tether entity approval.
No on-chain queued redemption or daily caps; off-chain redeem has min ~430 XAUt (1 bar) + 25bp fee + delivery, processed in business days after KYC[](https://gold.tether.to/faq).
No forced-exit, escape-hatch, or permissionless emergency exit for adversarial admin; blocked addresses can have funds destroyed by multisig with no recourse on-chain.
On-chain transfers directly callable via any wallet/Etherscan write tab (ERC-20 standard, no frontend required); off-chain physical redeem requires official app + KYC.

steelman.red: No on-chain exit to principal (physical gold claim); admin (multisig) can indefinitely blocklist and destroy user funds with no time cap or escape hatch; redemption requires Tether entity KYC/approval — users cannot exit on their own terms under adversarial conditions.
steelman.orange: On-chain token transfers remain permissionless even if blocked (no transfer hook revert per vuln report and ABI); off-chain redemption path exists with documented process (though gated).
steelman.green: ERC-20 transfers are fully permissionless and directly callable; no pause on transfers; independent wallet/DEX paths exist for moving tokens.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because there is no on-chain exit function for the gold claim (E1/E6), admin can destroy blocked funds indefinitely (E3), and physical redemption requires off-chain KYC+approval by the issuer with no permissionless escape hatch (E2/E4/E5), meeting multiple red criteria despite permissionless transfers.

evidence.shows: Implementation ABI: transfer/transferFrom/approve (permissionless), mint/blocklist/destroyBlockedFunds (owner-only), no paused() or redeem function for users.

Redemption for physical gold/USD requires KYC verification, login to Tether app, min 430 XAUt per bar, 25bp fee + delivery; US persons prohibited; processed off-chain by TG Commodities after approval.
No on-chain redeem or exit mentioned; all physical redemption and purchase handled by TG Commodities entity with KYC.

unknowns: E3: exact transfer behavior for blocked addresses not re-read on-chain (possible hook or not); assumed not fully blocking transfers based on ABI and prior vuln report.
E6: no escape hatch or permissionless emergency exit discovered after full ABI and website review.

headline: ~100% TVS exposed to single issuer (Tether/TG Commodities) failure: physical gold custody, reserves attestation (BDO), and off-chain redemption processing; no on-chain oracles/fallbacks or cross-module diversification

findings.text: No external contract calls, oracles, price feeds, or on-chain dependencies in core token contracts (pure ERC-20 + owner controls; no getPrice/latestAnswer/chainlink in ABI or reads across ETH/ARB/POLY proxies).

Off-chain issuer committee (TG Commodities S.A. de C.V. + Tether) controls mint, reserves allocation, redemption approval, and physical gold custody in Swiss LBMA vaults; no on-chain validator set or reporter committee.
No material bridge dependencies for core TVS (separate deployments on ETH/ARB/POLY; no canonical bridge carrying significant bridged TVL mentioned; cross-chain is not required for primary use).
No nested collateral/restaking; direct 1:1 claim on physical gold bars (no LRT depth or propagation beyond issuer).

No on-chain fallback, circuit breaker, sanity check, or second-oracle for any external input (none exist); reserves attested quarterly by BDO Italia (reasonable assurance on reserves report only, not full SC or company audit; https://gold.tether.to/reports). Fallback status: DOCUMENTED only.
Multisig can upgrade implementation (potentially introduce new external calls/dependencies) with no timelock or exit window for users (C2 evidence).

steelman.red: 100% of TVS is a claim on physical gold held/custodied/attested/redeemed solely by Tether entity and Swiss vaults; issuer failure (insolvency, non-redemption, reserves shortfall, or hack) directly impairs principal with no on-chain mitigation, fallback, or diversification.
steelman.orange: On-chain token remains transferable and tradable on DEX/CEX regardless of issuer status; quarterly BDO reserves attestation provides some transparency; multiple chain deployments reduce single-chain risk.
steelman.green: No on-chain oracles or external contract dependencies in the token logic itself; backing is direct allocated physical gold with public serial-number verification on website.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because the entire protocol is a single-issuer RWA claim (A2/A6/A9) with no on-chain fallback or mitigation (A1/A6), and issuer failure can cause loss of principal (gold claim), meeting red criteria; impacted TVS ~100%.

evidence.shows: No external calls, oracles, or dependencies in ABI or state; pure token with owner controls only.
Quarterly reserves reports attested by BDO Italia (reasonable assurance on gold reserves only); gold held in Swiss LBMA vaults by custodian; no on-chain oracle or automated fallback.
All mint/redeem/physical delivery processed off-chain by TG Commodities (Tether entity) after KYC; no on-chain exit or fallback mechanism.

unknowns: A2: exact legal entity structure and diversification of Swiss vault operators unknown beyond BDO attestation; assumed single-issuer dependency.
A9: whether upgrade can introduce new external dependencies not re-verified beyond proxy upgrade capability.

headline: On-chain transfers/approvals fully permissionless with no contract whitelist/KYC or operator approval; independent paths via any wallet/DEX exist; KYC/US ban and ToS are off-chain frontend/issuer policies only

findings.text: No whitelist/allowlist/onlyWhitelisted/isKYCed/isAccredited modifiers or role checks on transfer/approve/transferFrom (standard ERC-20 in implementation ABI; https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x4c0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566).
No off-chain operators or committees required to admit on-chain transfers or approvals; mint and physical redeem require off-chain KYC/issuer approval but are not on-chain admission gates.

Frontend (app.tether.to) requires KYC for purchase/redeem and explicitly prohibits US persons (ToS quote: 'U.S. persons are prohibited from purchasing or redeeming XAU₮'); compliance discretion stated. This is A3-active on official UI only.

Independent paths exist: any EVM wallet (MetaMask etc.) for direct contract calls; DEX aggregators/wallets route through ERC-20; published contract address on Etherscan/CoinGecko enables third-party frontends and SDKs (no official SDK required but permissionless access confirmed).

On-chain blocklist exists (addToBlockedList/destroyBlockedFunds by owner) but does not gate entry/transfers (no transfer hook revert; prior vuln report confirms transfers from blocked possible); not a full on-chain sanctions blocklist for admission.
Read access fully permissionless (anyone can query balance/totalSupply); write access for transfers/approvals also permissionless; only mint/blocklist/destroy gated to owner.

ToS[](https://gold.tether.to/legal/termsofservice) contains jurisdictional/sanctions clauses (US prohibited, compliance discretion); verbatim extraction not performed due to SPA but policy acknowledged in FAQ.

steelman.red: KYC mandatory for purchase/redeem + explicit US person ban + issuer discretion + on-chain blocklist updatable by multisig creates effective admission gate for core value accrual.
steelman.orange: Official frontend enforces KYC and geo/compliance; no published official SDK or third-party frontend documented by protocol itself.
steelman.green: Core contracts impose zero whitelist/KYC/operator gate on transfers/approvals (A1/A2); blocklist does not prevent transfers (A4); multiple independent paths (wallets/DEX) exist (A3b); frontend policies are non-determinative per rubric.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because contracts are fully permissionless for user entry/exit (transfers), no contract-level KYC/whitelist (A1), no on-chain operator approval required for admission (A2), and independent paths via wallets/DEX exist (A3b), with KYC/US ban being off-chain issuer/frontend policy only (A3/A6).

evidence.shows: ERC-20 transfer/approve functions have no access modifiers or whitelist checks; only owner-gated mint/blocklist/destroy.
KYC required for buy/redeem via official app; US persons prohibited; off-chain process by TG Commodities; on-chain token use not restricted.
Token is standard ERC-20; tradable 24/7 on exchanges; no contract-level admission gates mentioned.

unknowns: A3b: exact list of third-party frontends/aggregators not exhaustively enumerated but existence confirmed via Etherscan/CoinGecko listings and DEX pool references.
A6: full verbatim ToS sanctions clause not extracted (SPA render); policy direction clear from FAQ.

headline: Bytecode verified on Etherscan/Sourcify (proxy + impl) with public contract addresses; no public source repo or recognized-firm smart contract audit; reserves attested by BDO (not SC audit)

findings.text: Ethereum proxy (0x68749665ff8d2d112fa859aa293f07a622782f38) and implementation (0x4c0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566) bytecode verified (defipunkd + Etherscan links show ABI/source available; Sourcify for Arbitrum proxy); 'Contract Source Code Verified' status confirmed via surfacers and Etherscan.
No matching public GitHub repo or commit found (protocol.github none recorded; web search returned no canonical Tether Gold source repo; only third-party tools/discussions).

No smart contract audit in protocol.audit_links or website; Etherscan shows 'No Contract Security Audit Submitted'. Reserves reports attested quarterly by BDO Italia (ISAE 3000 reasonable assurance on gold holdings only, not SC or full audit; https://gold.tether.to/reports).

BDO Italia (recognized accounting firm for attestations) but not a recognized Solidity SC auditor (Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin, PeckShield, etc.); no SC audit from recognized firm covering deployed contracts.
No post-audit drift analysis possible (no baseline audit); historical vuln (BlockSec 2025 transferFrom issue) reported and fixed per public disclosure, but no recent recognized re-audit.
Proxy verified with implementation verified separately (both surfaced and readable on defipunkd/Etherscan).

steelman.red: No public source repo and no recognized SC audit means outsiders cannot independently verify intended behavior beyond bytecode match; reserves attestation is accounting-only, not code.
steelman.orange: Bytecode fully verified on explorers for proxy+impl across chains; contract addresses public and ABI readable; BDO reserves attestation provides some transparency on backing.
steelman.green: All main contracts verified on Etherscan/Sourcify with no 'unverified implementation' gap; public deployment addresses enable independent inspection.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because bytecode is verified (V1/V6) but no public source repo (V2) and no recognized-firm SC audit covering deployed contracts (V3/V4), with only accounting attestation for reserves — meets orange criteria exactly.

evidence.shows: Proxy verified (TransparentUpgradeableProxy); implementation address surfaced and separately verifiable.
Implementation verified; full ABI and source available via explorer/Sourcify.
Contract Source Code Verified; no audit submitted.
Quarterly BDO Italia attestation on reserves (ISAE 3000); not a smart contract audit.

unknowns: V2: no commit SHA or repo match possible; no public source repo exists per exhaustive search.
V3/V4: no SC audit from recognized firm; BDO is reserves attestation only (not code review).
